chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who travels in the month of Ramadan and has a female servant with him, is it permissible for him to have intercourse with her during the day? He said: Glory be to Allah, does he not know the sanctity of the month of Ramadan? For him there is a long night. I said: Is it not permissible for him to eat, drink, and shorten (prayer)? He said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, granted permission to the traveler to break the fast and shorten (prayer) as a mercy and to alleviate the burden of fatigue, exertion, and difficulty of travel, but He did not grant him permission for intercourse with women while traveling during the day in the month of Ramadan. So He made it obligatory upon him to make up the fasting, but did not make it obligatory upon him to complete the prayer when he returns from his journey. Then he said: And the Sunnah is not to be measured (by the ruling of the traveler), and indeed when I travel in the month of Ramadan, I do not eat all the food nor drink all the drink.
ai.seo_question: Can a traveler in Ramadan have sexual intercourse during the day, and what are the consequences?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the distinction between the concession of breaking the fast (iftar) and the prohibition of sexual intercourse (jima') during daylight hours for travelers in Ramadan. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that while travel permits shortening prayers and eating/drinking, it does not exempt one from the sanctity of the month regarding intimacy, thereby requiring only qada (making up the fast) rather than kaffarah (expiation). The Imam further illustrates the concept of 'Sunnah not being measured by rulings' by noting his personal practice of continuing to eat and drink fully while traveling, highlighting the flexibility within the legal framework.
